Welcome to my page! I am a Research Biostatistician at [Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center](https://www.mskcc.org/) in New York City. My current collaborations involve working with hepatic pancreatic biliary (HPB) surgeons, melanoma medical oncologists, and global breast cancer research physicians. I have experience in design and analysis of clinical trials and observational studies (retrospective and prospective). I specialize in conducting statistical analysis and visualization using both R and SAS programming languages.

I earned my MSPH in Biostatistics at Emory University's Rollins School of Public Health. While obtaining my degree, I conducted research for the Centers for Disease Control, Emory's Biostatistics Collaboration Core, and professors with appointments in the Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Department of Epidemiology, and Winship Cancer Center. Prior to graduate school, I worked for Statistics Collaborative (now WCG Statistics Collaborative) in Washington, DC providing support for data monitoring committees.

In my free time, I enjoy traveling, reading, riding my Peloton, and playing the many games available on the New York Times Games app.
